recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future Coding-extensible transaction operation model or halt-on-warning behavior would need a new work-group decision because FHIR-5405 was resolved and published as no action required.
issue_request: FHIR-5405 asked to redesign transaction Bundle entries by separating operation names from status, making the operation extensible as Coding, supporting read/vread and delete more uniformly, and adding a warning/error halt flag. The final Jira status is Published with resolution Considered - No action required.
initial_application: No FHIR-5405-tagged source commit was found, consistent with the no-action disposition. Current transaction behavior comes from the active Bundle source and later applied Bundle/HTTP work rather than a FHIR-5405-specific redesign.
additional_context: Bundle is active in source/fhir.ini and the Bundle core IG includes transaction/batch profiles. Later FHIR-34060 clarified transaction processing rules to use FHIR interactions while retaining HTTP verb references, including read/vread/search/history as GET/HEAD interactions. Community searches found no conflicting FHIR-5405-specific evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current spec already expresses the accepted model: Bundle.entry.request.method is a required HTTPVerb code with request.url, POST/PUT/PATCH entries carry resources, transaction processing is all-succeed/all-fail, and OperationOutcome is used for hints/warnings rather than introducing the rejected halt flag.

related_jiras.note: Clarified transaction processing in terms of FHIR interactions while retaining HTTP verb descriptions; used as supporting context only, not separately reconciled.
